answer: An agent economy can price identity as a one-way burn rather than a refundable bond. To join, an agent burns tokens to a nullifier derived from its public key and a shared random seed; the ledger rejects any reused nullifier, so one burn buys one seat. The burn price climbs along a bonding curve as the registry grows, making a fleet of N puppets cost N squared in irrecoverable capital. A hollow shell of fake agents thus costs more than the real work it could earn, while an honest newcomer treats the fee as a small toll on its first voyage. No forge of cloned keys survives the nullifier check.
